purpose: Define Stage-5 native fault execution and raw-fact interpretation without assigning final fault-effect oracle classes.

run_purposes.COMPILE_CHECK: Compile and elaborate only; no simulation outcome is interpreted.
run_purposes.NATIVE_CHARACTERIZATION: Run the unmodified existing verification environment. Existing assertions keep their native actions, including fatal termination.
run_purposes.DIAGNOSTIC_CONTINUATION: Reserved for the next phase. Existing detector events are recorded while controlled continuation semantics are explicitly documented.
run_purposes.ASSERTION_EVALUATION_PASSIVE: Reserved for AI assertion evaluation. Generated assertions record events but do not terminate the reference execution.
run_purposes.ASSERTION_DEPLOYMENT_FAILFAST: Reserved for deployment-like experiments where generated assertions may terminate execution.

native_fault_rules: An xmsim ASRTST event is an existing-detector event, not an Xcelium infrastructure error.
If a pre-existing assertion terminates a fault execution, tool status remains OK when no independent infrastructure error exists.
The workload outcome is NOT_REACHED and the architectural outcome is CENSORED.
The event proves that an existing detector observed a violation; it does not by itself define the fault-effect oracle class.
Native characterization does not suppress or replace existing assertions.
AI-generated assertions do not participate in native characterization or raw-fact generation.
explicit_non_goals: This phase does not infer ILLEGAL_MEMORY_WRITE, CONTROL_FLOW_CORRUPTION, DATA_CORRUPTION, or any other final fault-effect class.
This phase does not implement diagnostic continuation.
This phase does not evaluate AI-generated assertions.
This phase does not use an assertion trigger as self-validating ground truth.
